rationale: Map view is explicitly outside the Phase 1 vertical slice. Planned as MapLibre plus pre-approved z0-z6 world PMTiles, which carry mandatory ODbL attribution. Satellite imagery archives are commercial or require accounts, so they stay an external handoff.

Depends on the map layer and on image intelligence, both of which land after the slice. Kokin stores a geospatial-precision confidence dimension from the start so geolocated claims have somewhere honest to record uncertainty.

Media intelligence - EXIF, pHash, near-duplicate clustering - is sequenced immediately after the graph view. Reverse image search against Google, Yandex, Bing and TinEye is out of scope as automated querying: see R-009 and docs/limitations/reverse-image.md.

Platform APIs are gated, paid, or prohibit automated collection. Phase 1 ships static HTTP fetch only, and every capture records capture_completeness=static_html_only so a partial snapshot is never mistaken for a full one.

Username enumeration is the intended first connector after the slice, via a declarative WhatsMyName-style sweep. Blocked on D-012: the WhatsMyName dataset is CC BY-SA 4.0, so adapting it into our own connector format creates a ShareAlike obligation. holehe is rejected outright - GPL-3.0 and unmaintained since 2024-09-10.

phase1_scope: http_fetch connector, HTML extraction to observations
rationale: This is the vertical slice. Ingest one URL, preserve the capture and its integrity metadata, extract title, OG tags and mailto/domain mentions as located observations. Domain and infrastructure research (DNS, RDAP, crt.sh) follows in Phase 2.

Corporate registry coverage is jurisdiction-specific and mostly behind paid aggregators. Depending on a paid service for a core workflow is a stated Phase 1 non-goal. Import-only via the connector SDK remains available to users who have their own access.
Conflict monitoring is a domain specialisation built on continuous collection at scale, which is a stated non-goal. Kokin is the workspace such data would be imported into, not the collector.
Flight and vessel tracking APIs are commercial with restrictive terms. Import-only.
Highly specialised datasets with no overlap with the Phase 1 reference workflow.

phase1_scope: content-addressed encrypted blob store, capture preservation
rationale: Kokin's L0 provenance layer is archiving: BLAKE3 content addressing, hash-on-write, and append-only capture records. Third-party archive services such as the Wayback Machine are a Phase 2 connector, not a Phase 1 dependency.

phase1_scope: three-layer data model, entity resolution, search workbench, activity history
rationale: This is the category Kokin actually competes in, and the competitor matrix shows why: the incumbents collapse evidence and conclusions into one graph. Separating L0 provenance from the L2 analytical layer is the product thesis.
